qualification: The essential educational qualification differs by fellowship code. For JRF-01 to JRF-03, two alternative qualification routes are given. For JRF-04, an M.Sc. in Physics with NET qualification is required. || Important points on qualification from the notification: || The GATE paper and the subject of the qualifying degree must be related to the subject / discipline against which the candidate is applying. || The NET / GATE score should be valid as on the date of interview in the aforementioned subjects. || Marks obtained in the qualifying exams must be mentioned as a percentage in the Excel sheet. Candidates need to submit a supporting document, issued by the concerned University, for converting CGPA / CPI to the equivalent percentage.

age_limit: The upper age limit for JRF is a maximum of 28 years as on the closing date of the interview. || The notification states that the upper age limit is relaxable for SC/ST by 5 years and OBC by 3 years, or as per Government guidelines. Use our Age Calculator to calculate your exact age as per the official cut-off date.
selection_process: The selection process in the notification has two main parts: shortlisting and an interview. || Shortlisting:Eligible candidates for the JRF interview will be shortlisted based on valid NET / GATE score for candidates having only B.E. / B.Tech. / M.Sc. degree, and based on percentage of marks in M.E. / M.Tech. for candidates having an M.E. / M.Tech. degree. || Interview:Shortlisted candidates will be called for an interview on a date to be intimated later. The venue is at Hyderabad. || Document verification:At the time of interview, candidates must produce original certificates for verification along with a set of self-attested copies of the certificates. || Applications without the required supporting documents will not be considered during shortlisting. Incomplete, unfilled or partially filled Excel sheets are liable for rejection and no intimation will be made in this regard. || The notification also states that the final decision on the award of fellowship is entirely at the discretion of the Selection Committee of the Lab, and that the management of DMRL reserves the right to amend, cancel or suspend the selection process at any time without assigning any reason.

title: Technical Graduate Course (TGC-145) Officer     – 30 Posts
qualification: B.Tech/B.E
salary: Fixed Stipend for Cadet Training:Rs. 56,100 per month (starting pay in Level 10 of the Pay Matrix) throughout training at IMA Dehradun. On successful commissioning, the officer's pay is fixed in the first cell of Level 10; the training period is not treated as commissioned service, but arrears of admissible allowances for the training period are paid to cadets. || Military Service Pay (MSP):Rs. 15,500 per month, fixed, for officers from Lieutenant to Brigadier rank. || Dearness Allowance:Admissible at the same rates and conditions as applicable to civilian personnel, from time to time. || Para Reserve Allowance:Rs. 2,625 per month. || Technical Allowance:Tier-I – Rs. 3,000 per month; Tier-II – Rs. 4,500 per month. || Field Area Allowances:Officers posted to Field Areas are eligible for allowances depending on rank and area of posting, ranging up to Rs. 42,500 (RH-Max) and including Siachen Allowance, High Altitude Allowance, Flying Allowance, Special Forces Allowance, and several other risk/hardship-linked allowances specified in the notification. These allowances apply strictly as per the laid-down qualification/eligibility conditions and are not admissible to everyone. || Dress Allowance:Rs. 20,000 per year. || Ration in Kind:In Peace and Field Areas. || Transport Allowance (TPTA):For Pay Level 10 and above, Rs. 7,200 per month plus DA in Higher TPTA Cities (Hyderabad, Patna, Delhi, Ahmedabad, Surat, Bengaluru, Kochi, Kozhikode, Indore, Greater Mumbai, Nagpur, Pune, Jaipur, Chennai, Coimbatore, Ghaziabad, Kanpur, Lucknow, Kolkata), and Rs. 3,600 per month plus DA at other places. This is not admissible where Government transport is provided; officers in Pay Level 14 and above can opt for an official car or Rs. 15,750 per month plus DA; not admissible for months fully covered by leave; physically disabled service personnel are paid at double rate, minimum Rs. 2,250 plus DA per month. || Children Education Allowance:Rs. 2,812.50 per month per child (per the Hindi text) / Rs. 2,250 per month per child (per the English text), for the two eldest surviving children, from pre-primary to Class 12. Reimbursement is once a year, after the financial year, on a certificate from the head of the institution. || Hostel Subsidy:Rs. 6,750 per month per child, for the two eldest surviving children, from pre-primary to Class 12. || Rates of Defence-specific allowances increase automatically by 25% each time Dearness Allowance rises by 50%, as per Government of India letter No. A-27012/02/2017-Est.(AL) dated 16 August 2017. || Pay, allowances and their rules/provisions are subject to revision from time to time.
age_limit: The age limit is 20 to 27 years as on 01 July 2027 , i.e. the candidate must be born not earlier than 01 July 2000 and not later than 30 June 2007.
